payload.name: Enumerate-person-activities-by-domain
payload.description: When a question asks for the complete set of a person's hobbies, interests, or free-time activities (e.g., 'what hobbies does X pursue?', 'what does X enjoy doing?') and a single memory search may miss diverse activity categories.
content: For enumeration questions about a person's hobbies or activities, do not answer after one search. First run a broad hybrid search using "<person> hobbies" or "<person> activities".
From the returned memories, list the distinct activity categories found (e.g., creative, outdoor, winter sports, reading, fitness).

Run additional targeted searches for uncovered common categories, using queries like "<person> outdoor activities", "<person> winter sports", "<person> reading", "<person> creative hobbies", and "<person> fitness".

After each targeted search, note any new activity categories. Stop when two consecutive targeted searches return no new categories, then synthesize the answer from the union of all retrieved memories.

solves: A single top-k memory search often misses semantically diverse memories when a question asks for the complete list of a person's hobbies, interests, or activities (e.g., sports, creative hobbies, reading, outdoor trips). Future questions like 'What hobbies does X pursue?' will again under-answer unless the agent searches by activity domain and checks coverage. This skill does not apply to questions about a single known activity (e.g., 'Does X like skiing?') where one targeted search suffices.
